Folks — reviewed Verde's proposed exclusion. My read and recommended position below.

Summary of Verde ask: carve out confidentiality breaches and "willful misappropriation of trade secrets" from the monetary cap; exclude injunctive/royalties from cap as remedies.

Red flags and risks:
- Unlimited exposure: an unqualified exclusion exposes us to open-ended claims and punitive/treble-style recoveries depending on jurisdiction.
- Definition gap: "trade secret" is often undefined; opponents can expand scope.
- Royalties/restitution language can morph into ongoing indemnity obligations.

Recommended counter-proposal (narrow):
1) "Notwithstanding Section X (Limitation of Liability), the liability cap shall not apply to damages arising from (a) a breach of the confidentiality obligations expressly identified in Section Y, and (b) willful and proven misappropriation of trade secrets, provided that such damages are limited to actual direct damages and not to consequential, incidental, punitive or exemplary damages."

Rationale: carves out the most legitimate customer concerns (confidentiality and willful theft) while capping exposure to direct economic loss. Explicitly disclaims consequential/punitive to preserve standard caps.

Additional protections to propose in parallel:
- Require claimant to produce demonstrable proof of willfulness and a narrowly drafted trade-secret definition (statutory definition + objective elements).
- Keep injunctive relief outside the cap (we can live with that).
- If Verde insists on royalties/restitution outside the cap, require these to be tied to adjudicated misappropriation (court/judgment) and subject to mitigation obligations.

I've attached a marked-up doc with suggested text (redline_suggestion.docx).

If you want me on the call with Client counsel, I can join.
